text:
kai: quick follow-up on the micro-lane proposals. new angle: autoscale micro-lane capacity per-host based on short-request load and recent pack_efficiency, with backpressure signals to clients. goal: keep p99 for chatty flows stable while bounding impact on batch efficiency and kv cache.

maria: autoscale micro-lane how? add/remove slots or adjust tenant_credits?

kai: both. two levers: host_slot_count and per-tenant_soft_credit. host_slot_count auto-increments when short_request_rate > threshold AND pack_efficiency > target. decrements slowly on sustained low util.

tj: sounds promising but risk of feedback loops. if we add slots we might increase kv_miss and reduce pack_efficiency, which would then remove slots -> oscillation. need damping.

kai: plan: use a PID-lite controller with an integration cap and a cooldown window. also require pack_efficiency above a hysteresis threshold to scale up. scale-down is conservative and uses long half-life.

anya: KV-cache consequence: if micro-lane grows it may fill KV miss budget. we should track a kvcache_miss_budget per-host and refuse upward scaling if miss_budget consumed.

lee: also tie autoscale to GPU utilization: if gpu_util is high, autoscale refuses to add slots even if short_request_rate is high. we don't want to starve throughput.

dev-sim: ran a sim overnight with mixed traffic. autoscale up fast, pack_efficiency dropped 8%, kv_miss +12% but p99 improved 45ms. when controller used pack_efficiency hysteresis the oscillation subsided. logs attached in sim.

maria: what about client-side backpressure? we can expose a 429-with-retry-after when micro-lane rejects due to quota, and a new header X-Redwood-ShortPath-Hint for clients to mark retries as long-payload-friendly.

kai: yes: two signals: 1) X-Redwood-Degraded when we routed to bulk, 2) 429 + Retry-After when we need clients to slow down small-request bursts. recommend SDK default to exponential backoff on that code.

tj: eviction policy question: when running low on headroom, do we steal micro slots or throttle new micro admissions?

kai: throttle new admissions first. steal only if emergency (gpu OOM risk) and log heavily. stealing will be admin-guarded behind a feature flag.

anya: telemetry additions: host.micro_lane.slot_count, host.micro_lane.scale_events, host.kvcache.miss_budget, host.pack_efficiency, short_request_429_rate. add alert when 429_rate > 0.5% sustained.

lee: rollout: feature-flag "micro_autoscale_v1". staged: dev -> staging sim -> 1% canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. track p99/p995, token/sec, cost_per_token, kv_miss_delta.

ops-bot: infra reminder: ensure we have admin kill-switch and a runbook entry for autoscale oscillation and OOMs.

kai: config sketch: 
```
micro_autoscale:
  short_rate_threshold_per_sec: 120
  pack_efficiency_min: 0.72
  kvcache_miss_budget_min_pct: 20
  gpu_util_ceiling_pct: 90
  scale_up_step: 8  # slots
  scale_down_step: 4
  cooldown_ms: 60000
  integration_cap: 256
```

maria: good. add per-tenant opt-out for autoscale and an admin throttle cap per-host.

kai: will add. also plan to require a sim run for any config change.

tj: tests: control-loop unit tests, blackbox sim with adversarial workloads, and an integration that verifies no OOMs when scale-up happens.

anya: docs: explain tradeoffs and provide recommended client SDK backoff behavior. include sample config values and how to opt-out.

lee: monitoring: new dashboard with host-level autoscale trends, scale events, 429 rates, kv_miss budget, and pack_efficiency heatmap. auto-escalate if pack_efficiency drops >10% for 10m.

kai: next steps: I'll prototype controller in runner, wire metrics, and open RFC PR with sims + control-loop tests. tagging @maria @tj for review before canary.

maria: SGTM. please include a cost delta table and tail percentiles.

ops-bot: reminder: update runbook with emergency disable command for feature-flag "micro_autoscale_v1".
